newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean president gives up jogging.
newsitem.headline: South Korean president gives up jogging.

text.p: South Korea's most famous jogger, President Kim Young-sam, has given up his early morning runs.

"President Kim quit jogging last week," an official at the presidential Blue House confirmed on Wednesday after newspapers splashed the story. "He has taken up swimming and walks around the presidential mansion."
Kim's doctors had been advising Kim, 69, that the daily jogging routine he had kept up for 30 years was too strenuous. "The president finally decided to listen," the official said.
Kim ran three to four km (1.8-2.5 miles) each day with 10 or so aides through the picturesque grounds of the Blue House.

He would set off at 6:00 a.m. in summer and 30 minutes later in other seasons. He shared a workout run with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Seoul in 1993 and in the South Korean island of Cheju in 1996. He accompanied Philippine President Fidel Ramos on a jog in 1994.
